note: Présenter centrally means present/show/introduce. 'To look' is not a safe bare-verb gloss, and candidacy normally appears in the reflexive se présenter.
proposed_english: to present; to show; to introduce; to submit; to stand/run as a candidate (se présenter)

note: Frapper centrally means hit/strike/knock; 'shake' is not a safe general gloss.
proposed_english: to hit; to strike; to knock; to affect

note: Compte is not only the noun account; the same common written form also means count/tally and is a finite form of compter ('counts; takes into account').
proposed_english: account; count; tally; counts/takes into account (verb form, context-dependent)

note: The current gloss omits two basic senses: pièce = room and coin, in addition to piece/play/part.
Bare offrir means offer/give/present; treating or buying for oneself is reflexive s'offrir. The current entry omits the core bare-verb meaning.
proposed_english: to offer; to give; to present; to treat/buy for oneself (s'offrir)

note: Sujet also functions as an adjective meaning 'subject to'; adjective POS is listed but its meaning is missing.
proposed_english: subject; topic; exam question/paper; cause/reason; subject to

note: Flic is informal/slang for a police officer/cop; the current list of English slurs is unnecessarily noisy and lacks a register label.
Seconde is both the noun 'second' (unit of time) and the feminine adjective 'second'. The adjective reading is common and missing.
The proper place name Plaisir is irrelevant here. The core common noun is plaisir = pleasure/enjoyment.
Pire means both worse and worst depending on construction and can be substantivized as 'the worst'.
The current entry omits the core meaning entirely. Lâcher means let go/release/drop; fail/chicken out are contextual or colloquial extensions.
proposed_english: to let go; to release; to drop; to abandon; to fail/give up (context-dependent)

note: Réveiller is transitive 'wake/awaken someone'; 'wake up' intransitively is se réveiller. The learner gloss should distinguish them.
proposed_english: to wake; to awaken; to wake up (se réveiller)

note: Drôle very commonly means funny/amusing and also strange/odd. The current gloss omits the latter basic sense and foregrounds dated noun senses.
proposed_english: funny; amusing; strange; odd; rascal/kid (dated noun use)

note: Faux also centrally means wrong/incorrect/fake, not only false; these are important learner meanings.
The senses 'afford' and 'take the liberty' generally occur in the reflexive se permettre; bare permettre means allow/permit/enable.
proposed_english: to allow; to permit; to enable; to afford/take the liberty (se permettre)

note: Lever is transitive raise/lift; se lever means get up/rise. The noun le lever also means rising/raising. The current gloss conflates these uses.
proposed_english: to raise; to lift; raising/rising (noun); to get up/rise (se lever)

note: Malade also functions as a noun meaning a sick person/patient; noun POS is listed but the noun meaning is absent.
The entry explicitly lists finite/imperative forms of rêver but POS says noun only. Rêve is both the noun dream and common verb forms ('dreams/dream!').
proposed_english: dream; dreams; dream! (forms of rêver, context-dependent)
proposed_pos: noun / finite verb form / imperative form

note: Lit is not only 'bed'; it is also the common third-person singular form of lire, 'reads'.
